findings.problem: The clause-split tokens are enumerated in §2.3.4 but the exact re.split pattern (ordering/escaping of multi-char connectives vs the single-char class, and \s+ guards) is left to the implementer.
findings.fix: Specify the compiled pattern, e.g. re.compile(r"\s+bhi\s+|\s+بھی\s+|\s+aur\s+|\s+اور\s+|[.ۄ!?،,\n]") with connectives before the char class and \s+ guards so ' aur ' does not clip inside words.

findings.problem: The len(alias)>=3 'alias in norm' substring test can over-match a short alias inside an unrelated word when run on a whole clause. Harmless for the driver but could create spurious discovery rows for other inputs.
findings.fix: Use a word-boundary check for the pure-substring branch while keeping exact id/alias equality: if len(alias)>=3 and (alias==norm or re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(alias)}\b", norm) or norm in alias). Optional.

findings.problem: The awaitability of AsyncConnection.exec_driver_sql and sync fetchall() on the pinned SQLAlchemy is flagged as an implementation-time confirmation but no decided fallback is stated.
findings.fix: Document the text()-wrapper alternative in §2.4.2: res = await conn.execute(text('PRAGMA table_info("complaints")')); cols = {row[1] for row in res.fetchall()}. Pick one at implementation time; both are additive and fail-fast.
